subject.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests

question: Should ClickClack use an unconditional 30-second completion deadline for JSON REST reads and mutating calls, with multipart uploads exempt, and is the resulting ambiguous-write outcome acceptable to the channel contract?
rationale: The patch is narrow and has prior controlled-server evidence, but choosing a permanent timeout and accepting timeout-after-send semantics is a channel reliability policy decision rather than a mechanical code correction.

options.title: Approve the bounded JSON REST policy
options.body: Accept the 30-second deadline for JSON reads and writes, retain the multipart exemption, and require current-head proof that the intended timeout behavior still holds.

options.title: Narrow the deadline scope
options.body: Apply the deadline only to idempotent reads or selected request classes until ClickClack write idempotency and retry behavior are explicitly defined.

options.title: Defer the behavior change
options.body: Keep the current request behavior until an owner defines a broader ClickClack timeout and retry policy.

recommendation.title: Approve the bounded JSON REST policy
recommendation.body: Accept the 30-second deadline for JSON reads and writes, retain the multipart exemption, and require current-head proof that the intended timeout behavior still holds.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR discussion directly asks this person to choose the permanent request-class and deadline contract.
